title: The Folly of the Flesh-Lovers
english: Only once does he call those who encounter him ants and worms, fleeting wisdom of temporary glory; but when he is snatched away from life and, like a slave of lashes, is deprived of those things of which through ignorance he thought himself a master, humility is imposed upon him in response to his pride. Like a goat putting forward the wails of a mourning woman, he calls upon the patriarch from afar and ignorantly, saying: 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus, so that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, for I am suffering in this flame' (Luke 16:24), seeking a mercy which was not given when it was easy for him to do good because he possessed the authority; and demanding that Lazarus arrive to help against the fire, praying to suck the finger of the leper slightly moistened with water. Such are the follies of the flesh-lovers; this is the end of the lovers of wealth and the lovers of pleasure.

And it is fitting for the prudent and the provident of the future, having taken as a parable something like a preventative medicine for a disease, to flee the experience of such evils, regarding compassion and philanthropy as the cause of life.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Severity of Divine Judgment
english: Regarding the discipline that is to come, having practiced it. For the word has dramatically set out the admonition upon specific persons, so that, having been taught the law of the good citizenship with life and demonstration, we might never despise the commands of the Scripture, fearing them only as far as a word, and not indeed leading the threat toward punishment.

For I know how many of men, being enticed by such insinuations, grant themselves the power to sin unhindered. But on the contrary, we are taught by the present Scripture that no forgiveness lightens the penalty of that judgment, nor does philanthropy diminish the appointed punishment, if it is necessary for the voices of the patriarch to confirm the word.

For having heard many supplications from the rich and a myriad of pitying voices, he was neither moved by the wailings nor did the pain depart from the one bitterly flogged, but with strict wisdom he ratified the righteous judgment, saying that God has allotted to each according to his worth; and to you, since you have lived in luxury according to the others...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Chasm and the Separation of Good and Evil
english: The justice of the trespass has been imposed upon you through three afflictions; but to the one there, having been toiled and trodden down and being vexed by the bitterness of the fleshly life, a certain sweet and rejoicing state has been distributed here.

Moreover, he says there is a great chasm, which prevents them from intermingling with one another, and it separates those punishing from those being punished, so that both may clearly distinguish themselves from one another, having an unmixed enjoyment of the good and the evil. I think the sensory parable is an enigma of an intellectual theory. For let us not truly suppose a ditch actually dug there among the angels, like the trenches that happen in military camps, but Luke describes to us the separation of those who are divided from one another, both those according to virtue and those who lived otherwise, setting forth the image of the chasm (Luke 16:26).

And Isaiah, saying something like this, seals our mind: Is not the hand of the Lord too weak to save, or has his ear become heavy so as not to hear? (Isaiah 59:1). But your sins divide you from one another and from God.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
